summary:
TerraTwin – Planetary Analog Explorer is an interactive educational platform connecting geological locations on Mars and the Moon with similar environments on Earth.

Because direct exploration of other planetary surfaces is limited, TerraTwin brings planetary and Earth geology information together to help users explore terrestrial analogues and their scientific value.

Users explore a 3D globe, select a location, and view its geological features. They can compare it with Earth locations through two approaches: terrain and shape (landforms and topography), or materials and characteristics (rocks, minerals and geological composition). The platform presents images, location details, geological descriptions, and related research activities.

Our research includes Nili Fossae, Eridania Basin and Dao Vallis on Mars, and Marius Hills and Schrödinger Basin on the Moon, alongside Earth examples such as Thingvellir in Iceland and the Semail Ophiolite in Oman.

TerraTwin supports scientific learning about rover mobility, geological sampling and mineral studies. Its creative approach combines interactive 3D exploration with two complementary comparison methods. An English and Arabic interface makes the content accessible to a wider audience.

The project was developed as a web-based platform using AI-assisted development tools. Future development may include more locations, scientific datasets and interactive exploration simulations.
